item.title: Explain Echoes From Scratch

turns.text: Make a 10-second vertical explainer with voice-over about why we hear echoes. Write the words yourself, keep it easy for kids, and choose the look.

item.tests: Tests autonomous short-script writing and delivery of a complete narrated explainer rather than a script-only response.

answer_sheet.Topic and audience: Why we hear echoes, explained simply for kids.

must_haves: One approximately 10-second vertical video includes intelligible English voice-over.
The narration explains that sound reflects off a surface and returns to the listener.
The visuals show sound traveling from a source to a surface and back toward the listener.
The explanation uses simple, child-friendly language and finishes without cutting off the narration.
The visual sound journey and the spoken explanation agree.

approvals.name: create_video_from_text

args.name: Why We Hear Echoes — Kids Explainer

style.prompt: Create a 10-second vertical kid-friendly educational explainer. Playful colorful 3D animation, soft rounded shapes, bright cheerful outdoor scene. One continuous clear medium-wide shot: a cute cartoon character stands well away from a large flat stone wall. The character calls toward the wall; show stylized glowing sound-wave rings traveling from the mouth to the distant wall, reflecting off the wall, and returning to the character's ear. Sound waves are illustrative visual aids. Keep the propagation and reflection clear, with outgoing and returning motion sequential, not simultaneous. Gently push camera in while keeping character and wall visible. A friendly warm off-screen narrator speaks in clear easy English, saying exactly: "An echo is sound bouncing back! Your voice travels to a wall, bounces off, and comes back to your ears." Fit this full narration naturally within 10 seconds. Narration only; no music, no extra dialogue. No on-screen text, no subtitles, no labels, no logos. Match the wave reflection to the narration. End with the character listening happily to the returning sound.
